name: screen_context.v1
description: The screen_context/v1 semantic IR (docs/07 §3): the ≤300-token, ≤20-component distillation of the live Compose semantics tree that SemanticSnapshotBuilder produces on-device. This is the SAME shape in three places that must never drift apart: the session_create_request.v1.json 'screen_context' field (docs/13 §2.1), the ctx.snapshot data-channel payload (docs/07 §6, docs/13 §4), and this file — this file is the one all three defer to. The tree's nesting, bounds, and geometry are deliberately absent (docs/07 §3 'Values over structure' — bounds were a rejected micro-alternative, ~40% of raw serialized bulk for zero agent value); the only structural fact kept is list/list_item containment, preserved positionally in the flat 'components' array (a list_item entry is one that immediately follows its list entry in reading order — docs/07 does not define a separate parent-id field, and none is invented here). additionalProperties is deliberately left unset throughout (docs/13 §9: new fields are additive within v1, same forward-compatibility posture as data_channel_envelope.v1.json and session_create_response.v1.json) — this is context telemetry the client produces, not a server-validated request body in the protocol/tools/*.json sense, so it does not take that file family's additionalProperties:false stance.

v.description: IR schema version marker. An unknown version is rejected by SnapshotIngestor's envelope check rather than by schema validation — but 'rejected' means the SNAPSHOT is dropped, not that the request fails: on the POST /v1/sessions path the response is still 201 and only the agent's context slot goes empty (docs/13 §2.1, backend/app/api/routes/sessions.py's _ingest_initial_screen_context). This description previously said '400 VALIDATION_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION'; that status is never produced here. docs/08 §7 has the reasoning — the pipeline degrades context, never conversation, because a merchant on a stale app build must still be able to start their support call.

screen.description: Screen identifier matching docs/01 §5's product-surface names (e.g. 'PaymentScreen'). Not a closed enum here: docs/01 owns the current five screens as a product fact, not a protocol constant, and new screens must not require a schema version bump (docs/13 §9).

flow.description: Nav-graph route group from NavigationTracker (docs/07 rule 7), e.g. 'vendor_payment'. May be empty '' for screens with no flow grouping (e.g. DashboardScreen) — the app-side AppContextState.kt default is flow = "", so the field is always present as a string, never absent or null.

components.description: Rank-and-capped component list, deterministic order (docs/07 rule 5): dialog/error_banner, then snackbar, then the focused field, then primary_cta/secondary_cta, then value-bearing fields/displays, then everything else in traversal order. Hard cap of 20 (docs/07 §3, §7) — the drop ladder (docs/07 §7) is what keeps a busy screen under this cap before the message is ever sent, so this is a true wire invariant, not just guidance.

last_action.description: Most recent EventTracker ring-buffer entry at capture time (docs/07 rule 7), or null before any action has occurred on this screen (e.g. the very first capture after a cold navigation). Always present as a key in a full snapshot — unlike a ctx.delta, which omits this key entirely when it did not change (docs/07 §6).

last_api.description: Most recent non-2xx response for this screen, from the core:network interceptor (docs/07 rule 7) — 'the single highest-value field in the IR'. null when no error has occurred on this screen. Always present as a key in a full snapshot, same rationale as last_action.

dirty_fields.description: testTag/label identifiers of editable fields with uncommitted edits (docs/07 rule 4) — 'the user typed a new amount but hasn't paid yet'. Empty array, never absent, when nothing is dirty (docs/07 §3 canonical example: 'dirty_fields': []).

loading.description: Set when any visible progress indicator survives pruning (docs/07 rule 4).

amount_field_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag 'amount_input' / suffix '_amount', else editable text matching a currency pattern.

value.description: e.g. '₹245'; '[REDACTED]' for sensitive field classes even though amount fields are not normally sensitive (docs/07 §5 rule 6).

focused.description: Carried only when true — the default (false) is omitted to save tokens (docs/07 §4 header note).

recipient_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag prefix 'recipient_'/'vendor_', else a contact-shaped row adjacent to an amount field.

primary_cta_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_cta', else the single filled Role.Button in the bottom action area. enabled is always carried explicitly (true or false) — unlike toggle's enabled, this is the headline fact for a CTA (docs/07 §3 canonical example carries 'enabled': true).

secondary_cta_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_secondary', else outlined/text buttons adjacent to a primary_cta.

text_field_component.description: docs/07 §4: SetText semantics with no more specific rule matching.

value.description: '[REDACTED]' for sensitive field classes: card number, CVV, PIN, Aadhaar, PAN (docs/07 §5 rule 6).

focused.description: Carried only when true (docs/07 §4 header note).

list_component.description: docs/07 §4: CollectionInfo semantics (LazyColumn/LazyRow). visible_count/total_count keep truncation honest when list_items are capped (docs/07 §7 rung 1, §8 'Long dynamic lists' failure row) — e.g. '3 of 47 settlement batches are visible'.

list_item_component.description: docs/07 §4: CollectionItemInfo child of a list; capped at 3 per list (docs/07 §4, §7 rung 1). The cap is a per-list count the builder enforces before transmission, not something this flat-array schema can structurally verify across a 'preceding list' boundary — enforced by the drop ladder and exercised by the dense fixture/tests, not the schema itself.

dialog_component.description: docs/07 §4: IsDialog / dialog window root; label from PaneTitle or first text run. visible is always carried (docs/07 §4 header note: transient roles carry visible even at its true default, because visibility is the headline fact) — the canonical fixture's 'Daily Limit Exceeded' dialog is this role.

snackbar_component.description: docs/07 §4: LiveRegion node inside a SnackbarHost; testTag suffix '_snackbar'.

toggle_component.description: docs/07 §4: ToggleableState semantics. value is the literal string 'on'/'off' (docs/07 §4 Carries column), not a boolean. enabled follows the general omit-at-default-true rule (docs/07 §4 header note) since a toggle's enabled state is not the headline fact the way a CTA's is.

balance_display_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_balance', else non-editable currency text outside a field.

status_badge_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_status', else chip-shaped node with enum-like text (SETTLED, PENDING, ...). value is free text here, not a closed enum — the doc gives examples, not a closed vocabulary, and per-business-domain status strings are exactly the kind of extension this schema must not freeze shut.

error_banner_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_error', else assertive LiveRegion outside a SnackbarHost. Ranked with dialog as the highest-priority interruption (docs/07 rule 5, tier 1).

alert_banner_component.description: docs/07 §4: testTag suffix '_alert' — dashboard notices; informational, not error.

image_component.description: docs/07 §4: icon/graphic WITH a ContentDescription and an OnClick (otherwise pruned per rule 1) — carries only label, no value/enabled/visible.

component.description: The docs/07 §4 role vocabulary — sixteen core roles, discriminated by 'role'. Deliberately closed to exactly these sixteen for the v1 freeze: docs/07 §4's 'Extension roles' paragraph describes per-app domain roles (collection_total, settlement_eta, batch_row, shortfall_flag, tracker_state, ...) registered declaratively 'in the same enum', but none of those extension names are pinned anywhere as a stable wire vocabulary (docs/01 §5's per-screen table is explicitly shorthand/non-authoritative per docs/07 §4). Widening this oneOf with additional per-role $defs is an additive, non-breaking change within v1 (docs/13 §9) when those extension roles are actually frozen by a future task — inventing wire names for them now would be guessing, not freezing.

last_api.description: docs/07 rule 7 shape: the most recent non-2xx response for this screen. error_code is the docs/13 §1.1 vocabulary, deliberately typed as a plain string rather than an enum here for the same reason signaling_message.v1.json's error payload does not enum 'code' — new codes may be added within a class without a version bump (docs/13 §1.1, §9).
